title: fix(spec)!: a book audience names one gate, and a gated book claims its pages by name
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuKG2Z9TG76Xqkusa81b3qqz)_

Fixes #37613

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: none — no `skills/` page teaches the book audience forms; `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx` documents both refusals in this change

DELIBERATE CORRECTION: `.changeset/36029-book-audience-system-permission.md` (pending, from #37591). Its sentence "an object that also carries `permissionSet` still parses as the older, non-strict `{ permissionSet }` arm with the other key dropped, as before." is false after this PR and now reads "and an object that also carries `permissionSet` is refused too: an audience names one gate." `Check Changeset` is red on this by design until the seat's record confirms it.

## 维护者速读

- 手册（book）的可见范围以后只能写一种门槛：同时写了「某个权限集」和「某项系统权限」会被直接拒绝，并告诉作者留哪一个。以前这种写法会悄悄只按权限集放行，作者以为是按系统权限。
- 设了可见范围的手册，如果用 `include: '*'` 把所有文档都揽进来，`os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` 和 Studio、REST、MCP 保存时都会报错，因为它会把不属于任何包的文档也藏起来。
- Setup 和 Studio 两个包各加了一个测试：它们注册的每篇文档都必须被自己的手册认领；文档名换了前缀、或手册改回 `'*'`，测试就会变红。
- 这是收严（narrowing），走 Tier H。存量数据不改写、开机也不拒；只有下次保存这类手册时才报错。仓库和 hotcrm 里没有一处这样写。

## What changes

- **`@objectstack/spec` — an audience names one gate.** `BookAudienceSchema`'s `{ permissionSet }` arm now declares `systemPermission` only to refuse it (`z.never`, message `BOOK_AUDIENCE_ONE_GATE`), and the `{ systemPermission }` arm moves from `.strict()` to `strictObject` with a `guidance` entry for `permissionSet`, so the union's chosen branch prints the same prescription. Rendered by `defineStack`:
  ```text
  ✗ books.0.audience: Unrecognized key(s) on this book audience: `permissionSet`.
    • A book audience names ONE gate, and this one names two: `permissionSet` and `systemPermission`. Keep `systemPermission` when the readers are everyone who holds a capability through any permission set (…); keep `permissionSet` when the readers are the holders of that one set. Delete the other key. …
  ```
  Only the second gate key is refused: `{ permissionSet, label }` still parses to `{ permissionSet }` exactly as before, and `{ systemPermission, label }` is still refused as before. Regenerated: `content/docs/references/system/book.mdx`. New upgrade-guide entry `book-audience-two-gates-and-catch-all-claim-refused` (ADR-0087 D3, notice only).
- **`@objectstack/lint` — `book-gated-catch-all-include` (error).** `validateBookAudienceClaims` refuses a book whose `audience` is `{ permissionSet }` or `{ systemPermission }` with a group whose `include` is the catch-all (a glob of `*` alone: `'*'`, `'**'`). Namespace globs, tag includes and pinned `pages` pass; `'org'` / `'public'` / no audience are out of scope. Registered `gating` on all three commands and on the runtime publish gate for `book` writes.
- **`@objectstack/setup`, `@objectstack/studio` — N4.** Each package gets `src/manual-claims-docs.test.ts`: it calls the plugin's own `start()` with a capturing manifest service, so it reads the docs and the book the package really registers, and resolves them with the spec's `resolveDocAudiences`. Every registered doc must carry exactly the manual's audience, and a control doc bound to no package must stay `org`. Wiring that came with it: a `test` script, `**/*.test.ts` dropped from `tsconfig.json`'s `exclude` so `typecheck` reads the tests (`check:type-check-coverage`), and a `vitest.config.ts` aliasing `@objectstack/spec/system` and `@objectstack/platform-objects/apps` to source (`check:test-source-alias`).
- **`packages/spec/liveness/book.json` — N5.** `name` goes back to `2026-09-27` (its evidence did not change in #37591); `audience` moves to `2026-11-27`, re-closed here against both refusals.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx` names both refusals where it already teaches the forms.

Decided in the thread (small, listed per the standing rule):
- **Route for item 1: the schema, not a lint rule.** Measured: `defineStack` parses a book at definition time, and `{ permissionSet: 'xy_admin', systemPermission: 'setup.access' }` comes out as `{ permissionSet: 'xy_admin' }` (probe against the built `dist` of `main` @ `adb65d16`). So for a TS config, the documented authoring path, every authoring rule receives the value with the key already gone, whatever its input tier (`authoring-rules.ts` § "What `normalized` does NOT buy" says the same). Only the runtime save door hands the rules the authored body. A lint rule would therefore miss the main path; the parse refusal reaches `defineStack`, `os validate` and the `/meta` save alike.
- **Narrow refusal, not a strict `{ permissionSet }` arm.** A strict arm refuses every stray key, and a stored book row is kept verbatim (`protocol-save.ts`: "Every other type keeps its body verbatim"), so nothing proves no stored `{ permissionSet }` audience carries some other stray key. The narrow form refuses only the pair the card names. The pair cannot have been meaningful in any stable release: `{ systemPermission }` first shipped in `19.0.0-next.0` (2026-11-26T19:13Z, after #37591 merged at 18:15Z); `latest` is `18.6.0`. A repo and hotcrm grep finds no audience with both keys (hotcrm's one gated book is `{ permissionSet }` claiming `crm_admin_*`).
- **What a stored two-gate row does after this lands** (source read, not measured): the docs gate lists stored books without re-parsing them, and `audienceAllows` reads `permissionSet` first, so such a row keeps the set gate it has today. The read-time diagnostics pass (`metadata-diagnostics.ts`) parses with the same schema, so Studio shows it as invalid; its next save is refused with the fix named.
- The catch-all rule is `gating` (error) and also runs at the runtime publish door, because a Studio, REST or MCP author of a book has no other door.
- The refusing key appears in the generated JSON schema as `"systemPermission": { "not": {} }` on the set arm, the same shape every `retiredKey` tombstone already emits (this schema's own `groups[].translations` among them).

## Why

Card #37613, three review follow-ups of #37591 / #37663: an audience written with both keys was accepted and silently gated on the set alone (an admin manual opening to a different group than its author meant); the authoring rule "a gated book never claims by `include: '*'`" was taught by the ADR-0046 §6.7 amendment and enforced nowhere; and nothing held the Setup and Studio docs to their manuals' name prefix.

## Tests

All run on this branch, head `8143254075`.

- `packages/spec` `src/system src/migrations src/shared src/kernel`: 191 files, 5601 passed. `book.test.ts` 52/52 (2 new: the two-gate refusal in both key orders with the prescription text; every shape accepted before still accepted, `{ permissionSet, label }` still stripped).
- `packages/lint` full suite: 241 files, 9749 passed. `validate-book-audience-claims.test.ts` 9/9: positive and negative pin per gated form, `'**'`, ungated audiences, map-shaped `books`, the three commands, and the runtime gate refusing a catch-all book write while passing a named claim. `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts` green with the new entry.
- `packages/apps/setup`, `packages/apps/studio`: 2/2 each; `typecheck` green in both and in `packages/lint`.
- `check:generated` (spec): all 14 current after `--fix` regenerated `book.mdx` only. `check:liveness`, `check:strictness-ledger` green inside it. `check:adr-0087-registration` green (registered). `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:changeset-fixed`, console-intercept disarm: green. eslint on every touched TS file: clean.
- Not run here: `rest`, `runtime`, dogfood and `ui/` suites (CI carries them; the only cross-package fixtures naming a catch-all are REST's catch-all control book, which is served through a stub, not a lint run).

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored, tree clean after)</summary>

- Spec: the refusing `systemPermission` field removed → `book.test.ts` 1 red (the two-gate refusal), 51 pass.
- Lint: the catch-all test disabled → 6 of 9 red.
- Setup: `include: 'setup_*'` → `'*'` → the control-doc pin red ("the manual claims a doc bound to no package").
- Setup: `setup_overview` renamed `admin_overview` → the claim pin red ("admin_overview is not claimed by setup_manual").

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- File surface vs the claim: the claim listed `packages/lint`, the pins, `liveness/book.json`, and `book.zod.ts` "only if the lint route cannot reach the authored value" — it cannot (above). Also touched: `packages/apps/{setup,studio}` (the N4 pins, their wiring), `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` (the ADR-0087 entry this narrowing owes), `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`, the regenerated `book.mdx`, and the pending `36029` changeset (DELIBERATE CORRECTION above). The claim's declarations were `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`; this PR declares `yes (narrowing)` / `narrowed`.
- A `public` book claiming by `'*'` also claims every doc bound to no package, and makes it anonymously readable. The ADR-0046 §6.7 rule names gated books only, so this rule does not refuse it; noted, not filed.
- The prescription arrives under the union's "Unrecognized key(s) on this book audience: `permissionSet`" line, because branch ranking prefers an unknown-key branch (`union-branch-policy.ts`); the bullet under it carries the whole fix.

## Verification

Read first: `packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts` (`BOOK_AUDIENCE_ONE_GATE`, `BookAudienceSchema`), then `packages/lint/src/validate-book-audience-claims.ts`, then `packages/apps/setup/src/manual-claims-docs.test.ts`.

Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run src/validate-book-audience-claims.test.ts` (9 passed) and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/setup test` (2 passed).

Tier H: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on `packages/spec/src`. Contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER owed by the seat; not self-reviewed here.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes (eslint on every touched file).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English.
